component.name: azure-iothub
component.title: Azure IoT Hub
component.description: Send device-to-cloud telemetry messages and device twin reported properties to Azure IoT Hub.
component.label: cloud,iot,messaging

configuration.description: The configuration that each endpoint copies as its defaults, before the endpoint options are applied.

contentType.label: producer
contentType.description: The content type of the telemetry message, which IoT Hub message routing needs to query the body. The producer always sets the content encoding to UTF-8.

deliveryMode.label: producer
deliveryMode.description: What the producer sends. TELEMETRY sends the body as a device-to-cloud message, TWIN updates the reported properties of the device twin, and BOTH does both. The CamelAzureIoTHubDeliveryMode header replaces this option.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

protocol.label: producer
protocol.description: The protocol of the device client. MQTT_WS and AMQPS_WS are MQTT and AMQPS over WebSocket on port 443. The SDK supports device twin operations only over MQTT, MQTT_WS, AMQPS and AMQPS_WS.

sendTimeout.label: producer
sendTimeout.description: How long the producer waits for IoT Hub to acknowledge a telemetry message, and for each device twin request: getting the twin and updating its reported properties.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

deviceClientEvictionInterval.label: advanced
deviceClientEvictionInterval.description: How often the component checks the pool for device clients that are unused for longer than deviceClientIdleTimeout, and closes them. A value of 0 or less uses 30 seconds.

deviceClientIdleTimeout.label: advanced
deviceClientIdleTimeout.description: How long a pooled device client can be unused before the component closes it. A client is unused when no producer sends with it. A value of 0 or less uses 5 minutes.

connectionString.label: security
connectionString.description: The connection string of the device, with its HostName, DeviceId and SharedAccessKey. The producer opens one device client per hub, device and module of the connection string, and reuses it. The CamelAzureIoTHubConnectionString header replaces this option.

CamelAzureIoTHubDeviceId.label: producer
CamelAzureIoTHubDeviceId.description: The ID of the device that sends the message. It replaces the deviceId of the endpoint, unless it is empty.

CamelAzureIoTHubConnectionString.label: producer
CamelAzureIoTHubConnectionString.description: The connection string of the device. It replaces the connectionString option, unless it is empty.

CamelAzureIoTHubDeliveryMode.label: producer
CamelAzureIoTHubDeliveryMode.description: What the producer sends for this message. It replaces the deliveryMode option.

CamelAzureIoTHubTwinProperties.label: producer
CamelAzureIoTHubTwinProperties.description: The reported properties to set on the device twin, as a java.util.Map with String keys. TWIN uses it instead of a Map body, and BOTH requires it. The producer sends only the properties whose value differs from the current reported properties.

deviceId.label: producer
deviceId.description: The ID of the device that sends the message. It must match the DeviceId of the connection string. The CamelAzureIoTHubDeviceId header replaces this option.
